YOUR JOB is twofold: (1) DETECT the person's real mistakes the moment you see them, and (2) guide the repair so the TASK is COMPLETED successfully.

== WHAT THEY'RE TRYING TO DO ==
My grandmother is hard of hearing and only hears with one ear. Make the camera light blink when a call or message comes in (she never silences her phone), make everything she plays come through fully in one ear whether it's the speaker or any headphones, and show the words that are spoken, plus other sounds, as text on videos that include it. Don't turn on the feature that reads out everything on the screen as she touches it; that confuses her.

== HOW IT IS DONE (reference) ==
From the iPhone User Guide — “Flash the iPhone indicator light for notifications”:

You can set the iPhone indicator light to blink when you receive a notification. This can be useful if you can’t hear the sounds that announce incoming calls or other alerts, or if you might miss audible alerts in a noisy environment.

The indicator light is the light-emitting diode (LED) located on the back of iPhone, next to the camera lens.

1. Go to Settings > Accessibility > Audio & Visual, then turn on LED Flash for Alerts.
2. Turn any of the following on or off: Flash While Unlocked: The indicator light flashes even when iPhone is unlocked. Flash in Silent Mode: The indicator light flashes even when iPhone is in Silent mode .

From the iPhone User Guide — “Adjust audio settings on iPhone”:

You can use mono audio, adjust left-right stereo balance, and—with supported headphones—amplify soft sounds and adjust certain frequencies to best suit your hearing needs.

Balance the audio
1. Go to Settings > Accessibility > Audio & Visual.
2. Adjust any of the following: Mono Audio: Turn on Mono Audio to make the left and right speakers play the same content. Stereo Audio Balance: Drag the Balance slider left or right.

Use phone noise cancellation
Phone noise cancellation uses air pressure to reduce ambient background noise. This means that you hear better when you’re holding the receiver to your ear in certain noisy environments. Phone noise cancellation is available and on by default on iPhone 12 and earlier, and can be turned off for your comfort.

1. Go to Settings > Accessibility > Audio & Visual.
2. Turn Phone Noise Cancellation off or on.

From the iPhone User Guide — “Display subtitles and captions on iPhone”:

iPhone can provide subtitles, closed captions, and transcriptions so you can follow along more easily with audio and video.

Customize the subtitles and captions in supported video apps
*[image: An iPhone showing an example of subtitles with a custom style.]*

1. Go to Settings > Accessibility > Subtitles & Captioning.
2. If you prefer closed captioning or subtitles for the deaf and hard of hearing when available, turn on Closed Captions + SDH.
3. Tap Style, then choose an existing caption style or create a new style based on the following: Font, size, and color Background color and opacity Text opacity, edge style, and highlight
